definitions.explanation: Something that already exists or is already in place, as opposed to something newly created. Almost always used attributively as {既存|きそん}の.

examples.japanese: {既存|きそん}の{制度|せいど}を{見直|みなお}す。
{新|あたら}しい{案|あん}は{既存|きそん}のものより{優|すぐ}れている。
examples.english: The new proposal is better than the existing one.

examples.japanese: {既存|きそん}の{建物|たてもの}を{壊|こわ}さずに{改装|かいそう}して{利用|りよう}する。
examples.english: We will renovate and use the existing building rather than demolishing it.

notes:
Composed of {既|き} (already) + {存|そん} (to exist). Refers to what already exists, in contrast to something new. Read きそん, though きぞん is sometimes heard colloquially.

USAGE:
Almost always used attributively, with の before a noun:
- {既存|きそん}のシステム: the existing system
- {既存|きそん}の{建物|たてもの}: an existing building
- {既存|きそん}の{顧客|こきゃく}: existing customers

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {現行|げんこう}: current; in force — used for rules and systems currently in effect
- {従来|じゅうらい}: conventional; up to now — emphasizes 'as it has been until now'
